summary: Iter-5 (Journey Runtime + POS Connectors) end-to-end validated. Backend: 24/24 pytest cases PASS in 58.6s including a real 60-95s poll that watches the background journey_worker execute a 2-step run (wait 0h → send_coupon 15%) and confirms it transitions pending→completed AND materialises a coupon in db.coupons with source='journey', code prefix 'JRN-', rules.usage_limit=1. Public /coupons/validate (no auth), Shopify (header + note_attributes), WooCommerce (meta_data + coupon_lines fallback), /pos/snippets (fully-qualified https URLs, correct topics, ≥3 instructions each), and purchase-trigger auto-enroll on /public/coupons/redeem all green. Frontend: /integrations renders pos-shopify + pos-woocommerce cards with correct https://…/api/pos/{ws}/shopify + …/woocommerce URLs, pos-curl visible with the generic curl command; /campaigns Enroll panel accepts an email, creates a run, and the recent-runs feed lists the new customer with status=PENDING and step 0/3 within ~2s.
ai_features_tested: AI Today's Promo / Weekly Calendar / One-Click / Segment Promo - not-in-scope-this-iteration (iter-5 does not touch AI code; per iter-4 handoff the EMERGENT_LLM_KEY is still budget-exhausted, we did not re-drive AI to preserve credits)

minor.issue: Response is not cached — request-level headers x-forwarded-proto/host are read every call; low-frequency admin route so fine, but consider a 60s cache.

No HMAC signature verification (documented as 'left to the merchant's account setup'). Any actor who knows the workspace UUID and a valid coupon code can forge a redemption + inflate stats.revenue. Recommend optional X-Shopify-Hmac-SHA256 verification using a per-workspace secret when the merchant configures it.

Same lack of signature check as Shopify — no X-WC-Webhook-Signature validation. Also, `coupon_lines` fallback takes the FIRST code without checking active state before _apply_from_pos handles it (safe, but redemption row is written with source='woocommerce' even for invalid codes → look at code path: `_apply_from_pos` returns applied=false without inserting a row, so this is actually OK — kept for reviewer awareness).

`email` field is EmailStr — passing a non-email customer id + email=null works (email=null falls back to None), but if caller sets email='' (empty string) pydantic will 422. Frontend currently sends `email: enrollFor.email || null` which is safe; document the requirement.
Fixed 30s sleep between polls means worst-case latency for a run with next_at=now is ~30s. For MVP fine, but a due-time signal (or `min(30, seconds_to_next_due)`) would reduce cold-start latency.

The generated coupon has `state='active'` and `audience: run.customer` (a single customer id/email), but there is no per-customer scope enforcement in `/public/coupons/redeem` — any actor who intercepts the JRN- code can redeem it as any customer. Combined with usage_limit=1 the blast radius is small, still worth logging.

No server-side validation of `steps[].type` — an unknown step type is silently logged as skipped ('unknown step type X') in the run log. Consider Pydantic Literal[...] validation to fail fast at create time.

issues: Console warning: 'The width(-1) and height(-1) of chart should be greater than 0' — chart parent lacks explicit minHeight so initial render logs 2x warnings before ResizeObserver settles. Same as iter-4.

Recent-runs feed shows step counter as 'step 0/3' after enrolling into a 3-step journey — expected while worker hasn't ticked yet, but there is no auto-refresh: user must close+reopen the enroll panel to see 'step 1/3', 'step 2/3', 'completed'. A polling refresh (every ~10s while the panel is open) or a manual 'refresh' button would improve UX.
Copy button on the webhook URLs is hidden behind a lucide icon with no tooltip/text — add title='Copy webhook URL' for accessibility.

action_items: OPTIONAL: HMAC signature verification for Shopify + WooCommerce webhooks (per-workspace shared secret) — currently anyone with workspace_id + a valid code can forge redemptions.
OPTIONAL: Auto-refresh the Recent runs feed on Campaigns page (poll every 10-15s while panel is open) so the user sees the run advance without clicking away and back.
OPTIONAL: Add Pydantic Literal validation for journey step types to fail fast at /journeys create.
OPTIONAL: Split /app/backend/server.py (now 2100 lines) into routers/ subpackage — same recommendation as iter-4.
critical_code_review_comments: server.py grew from 1752 → 2100 lines; still no router split. Every iteration compounds this — recommend routers/{auth,coupons,public,pos,journeys,ai,growth,loyalty,gift_cards,customers,api_keys,templates}.py before adding more surface.

journey_worker() runs forever with no supervised health/liveness signal. If it dies (exception outside the try — e.g. Motor client GC), nothing restarts it until a supervisor bounce. Consider exposing a /internal/journey_worker_health endpoint that checks `last_tick_at` written by the worker.

_execute_journey_step catches ALL Exception and stashes str(e)[:200] into log_entry['error'] but still advances current_step. A failing send_email will therefore silently skip that customer's email step forever. Consider a retry counter and 'failed' terminal status after N attempts.
gen_qr(...) is invoked on every journey-generated coupon; QR is a base64 PNG blob inline in the coupon doc — inflates Mongo docs and network payload of GET /coupons. Same concern as iter-4.

_apply_from_pos always uses currency ONLY from payload — but the coupon's discount_value is a raw number with no currency dimension. If a merchant sends EUR orders to a workspace that thinks in USD, stats.revenue is currency-mixed. Document or normalize.

public_validate only checks state=='active' + min_cart but ignores end_date / start_date. Expired coupons in state=active (state was set active but end_date is past) would still validate. Recommend comparing rules.end_date against now.

The Shopify/Woo webhook handlers accept any Content-Type as JSON via request.json() — a form-urlencoded body would 400 with a Pydantic-less bare 400. Test coverage exists for JSON path only; consider explicit Content-Type check + friendly 400.
PublicRedeem still stores customer plaintext (email/UUID) in redemptions + fires _fire_trigger which enrolls plaintext customer in journey_runs. PII concern persists from iter-3.

success_rate.backend: 100% (24/24 iter-5 pytest passed — 12 iter-5 specific + 12 regression smokes covering journeys/enroll/runs, worker, public validate/redeem, Shopify + Woo webhooks, /pos/snippets, dashboard, coupons, customers, gift-cards, store-credits, loyalty)
success_rate.frontend: 100% (Integrations pos-shopify + pos-woocommerce cards render with correct https://…preview URLs, topics, instructions, generic_curl; Campaigns enroll flow — journey-enroll-btn→panel→customer→submit→recent-runs — works end-to-end and shows PENDING status within 2s)

context_for_next_testing_agent: Iter-5 backend is fully green — journey_worker runs as an asyncio task from server startup (line 2092 of server.py) and ticks every 30s. Test suite `/app/backend/tests/test_iter5_features.py` covers all 8 iter-5 review items and can be re-run any time with `REACT_APP_BACKEND_URL=https://campaign-hub-436.preview.emergentagent.com pytest tests/test_iter5_features.py`. Two long-running tests (test_worker_executes_wait_and_send_coupon at ~60-95s poll, test_redeem_enrolls_in_purchase_journey at ~15s poll) are network+time-dependent; if flaky, increase the poll windows. rca of the issue: N/A — no defects found in iter-5 surface. The five initial regression assertion failures during a first-cut of the pytest file were AUTHOR ERROR (I asserted the endpoints returned bare lists when they in fact return richer summary objects — `/customers` returns {total,by_segment,customers[…]}, `/gift-cards` returns {total_issued, total_balance, outstanding, redeemed, gift_cards[…]}, `/store-credits` returns {total_outstanding, by_customer, credits[…]}, `/loyalty` returns {config, total_members, total_points, by_tier, members[…]}, and there is no `/experiments` top-level list route — experiments are per-coupon at /coupons/{cid}/experiments). Test assertions were corrected; the endpoint contracts themselves are consistent with iter-4 and were never broken.
